title: Dependencies can only be asked about one item at a time

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`graph.py` gives `dangling`, `cycles` and `blocked_by`. There is no reverse index — 
`ops.dependents` rescans every item linearly — no transitive closure and no topological
sort. `slicer next` answers "what should I do now" for exactly one item; `verify` answers
"is the graph valid".

Nothing answers "what is unblocked right now", "what does finishing S04 unblock", or
"show me the graph". Planning work is exactly those questions, and an agent planning a
batch has to reimplement them from `list --json`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
`slicer deps [ID] [--json]`: with an id, what it waits on and what waits on it; without,
every unblocked open item. A `--format mermaid` or DOT output would make the graph
reviewable in a pull request. Build the reverse index once per load in `graph.py`.

**Not in this slice:** scheduling or critical-path analysis.
